title: A fully faithful infinity-functor is equivalent to its full essential image
statement: Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use the coherent functors, full subcategories, mapping spaces and functor equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $J:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a coherent functor of infinity-categories which is fully faithful, meaning that $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal X}(x,x')\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal Y}(Jx,Jx')$ is an equivalence for every $x,x'\in\mathcal X$. Let $\mathcal Y_0$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal Y$ whose objects are precisely those $y$ for which there exist $x\in\mathcal X$ and an equivalence $y\simeq Jx$ in $\mathcal Y$. The restricted functor $J_0:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y_0$ admits a coherent quasi-inverse $K:\mathcal Y_0\to\mathcal X$, with coherent natural equivalences $KJ_0\simeq1_{\mathcal X}$ and $J_0K\simeq1_{\mathcal Y_0}$.

source.place: Kerodon, Theorem 4.8.4.1 (Kerodon Tag 01JX), applied to the functor with codomain its full replete essential image. This is a Kerodon identifier, not Stacks Tag 01JX.

proof.text: Work in a containing universe in which the simplicial sets $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ and their mapping spaces are small, with a further universe for their functor categories; this is a change of size convention, not a smallness hypothesis on the original categories. Apply [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] with $K=\Delta^0$, so $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal Y)=\mathcal Y$ by its simplicial definition: the full subcategory $\mathcal Y_0$ is a quasicategory. The full-subcategory definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] makes $J$ factor as a simplicial functor $J_0:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y_0$: every vertex $Jx$ belongs to the stated object class. For objects $u,v$ of $\mathcal Y_0$, every right-pinched mapping simplex between them has only the vertices $u,v$, so it lies in $\mathcal Y_0$ exactly when it lies in $\mathcal Y$. Thus the two mapping simplicial sets are equal. In particular $J_0$ is fully faithful by the given hypothesis on $J$.

source.place: Theorem 4.8.4.1, specialization to the full essential image; agent verification of the full-subcategory and universe conventions.

proof.text:
For each $y\in\mathcal Y_0$, its defining property supplies $x_y\in\mathcal X$ and an equivalence edge $e_y:y\to J_0x_y$ with inverse $d_y:J_0x_y\to y$. For every $z\in\mathcal X$, consider
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal X}(x_y,z)\xrightarrow{J_0}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal Y_0}(J_0x_y,J_0z)\xrightarrow{e_y^*}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal Y_0}(y,J_0z),\qquad e_y^*(a)=a\circ e_y.$$
The first map is an equivalence by Step 1. Use the composition maps and their homotopy classes in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] for the second map and for $d_y^*(b)=b\circ d_y$. Associativity, dependence of precomposition on the component of its edge, and the two inverse-triangle witnesses give homotopies on the entire mapping spaces
$$d_y^*e_y^*(a)=(a\circ e_y)\circ d_y\simeq a\circ(e_y\circ d_y)\simeq a\circ1_{J_0x_y}\simeq a,$$
$$e_y^*d_y^*(b)=(b\circ d_y)\circ e_y\simeq b\circ(d_y\circ e_y)\simeq b\circ1_y\simeq b.$$
The equalities of homotopy classes here are simplicial homotopies with Kan targets, in the convention of the cited node. Thus $d_y^*$ is a simplicial homotopy inverse for $e_y^*$. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] to conclude that $e_y^*$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The composite is consequently an equivalence of spaces (the induced component bijections and based homotopy-group isomorphisms compose). It is exactly $v\mapsto J_0(v)\circ e_y$, the universal-arrow map required next. These objectwise choices have not been asserted to form a functor.

source.place: Composition and precomposition, Construction 4.6.8.9 and Notation 4.6.8.15; agent inverse-homotopy calculation verifying the hypotheses of the local adjoint criterion, Kerodon 6.2.6.1 (02FV). Realization weak-equivalence implication: Kerodon 3.1.7.13 (00UB).

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion] to $R=J_0:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y_0$ and the arrows of Step 2. Both categories are quasicategories by the hypothesis and Step 1, and the displayed universal-arrow map has just been proved an equivalence for every $y,z$; no completeness, presentability or colimit assumption is used. The criterion supplies a coherent left adjoint $K:\mathcal Y_0\to\mathcal X$, a coherent unit $\eta:1_{\mathcal Y_0}\to J_0K$, a coherent counit $\epsilon:KJ_0\to1_{\mathcal X}$, and the triangle homotopies. In particular for $x,z\in\mathcal X$ it supplies the equivalence
$$A_z:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal X}(KJ_0x,z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal Y_0}(J_0x,J_0z),\qquad v\longmapsto J_0(v)\circ\eta_{J_0x}.$$
The transformations and their coherences are supplied together by the cited criterion, rather than assembled from independent objectwise lifts.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.6.1 and Proposition 6.2.1.17 (02F1), with the explicit induced mapping-space equivalence.

proof.text:
Every counit component $\epsilon_x:KJ_0x\to x$ is an equivalence. Write $q=KJ_0x$. On components of the mapping spaces, the triangle identity and the formula in Step 3 give
$$[A_z]\bigl([u]\,[\epsilon_x]\bigr)=[J_0u]\,[J_0\epsilon_x]\,[\eta_{J_0x}]=[J_0u].$$
Here components and their composition form the homotopy categories provided by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. The maps $[A_z]$ are bijective by Step 3, and $[u]\mapsto[J_0u]$ is bijective by Step 1. Hence precomposition with $[\epsilon_x]$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathcal X}(x,z)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathcal X}(q,z)$ for every $z$. Taking $z=q$ gives $r:x\to q$ with $[r][\epsilon_x]=1_q$. Taking $z=x$ and using injectivity, the equation $([\epsilon_x][r])[\epsilon_x]=[\epsilon_x]=1_x[\epsilon_x]$ gives $[\epsilon_x][r]=1_x$. Every component is represented by an edge, and the invertible-component criterion of the cited node turns these two equations into inverse-edge witnesses. Thus $\epsilon_x$ is an equivalence. This is an explicit two-sided inverse argument, not an invocation of a further Yoneda lemma.

source.place: Agent calculation with the induced adjunction equivalence; the counit inverse is proved explicitly in the homotopy category.

proof.text:
The triangle identity gives $[J_0\epsilon_x][\eta_{J_0x}]=1_{J_0x}$. A simplicial functor preserves equivalence edges by applying itself to the inverse edge and its two triangle simplices. Thus $J_0\epsilon_x$ is an equivalence by Step 4, and this equation makes $\eta_{J_0x}$ its inverse in the homotopy category. For any $y\in\mathcal Y_0$ choose $e:y\to J_0x$ as in Step 2. Naturality of the coherent unit gives
$$[J_0K(e)][\eta_y]=[\eta_{J_0x}][e].$$
Both $e$ and $J_0K(e)$ are equivalences, as is $\eta_{J_0x}$. Multiplying by the inverse of $[J_0K(e)]$ shows $[\eta_y]$ is invertible. The invertible-component criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] makes every $\eta_y$ an equivalence edge. The same calculation works when there are no objects, since then there is no component to check.

source.place: Agent extension from image objects to the replete essential image, using naturality and the adjunction triangle identities.

proof.text: The coherent counit and unit supplied in Step 3 have equivalence components by Steps 4 and 5. Apply the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal X,\mathcal X)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal Y_0,\mathcal Y_0)$. It makes $\epsilon:KJ_0\to1_{\mathcal X}$ and $\eta:1_{\mathcal Y_0}\to J_0K$ equivalences in these functor quasicategories. Hence $\epsilon$ and the inverse of $\eta$ are the required coherent natural equivalences $KJ_0\simeq1_{\mathcal X}$ and $J_0K\simeq1_{\mathcal Y_0}$. In particular $K$ is a coherent quasi-inverse on the whole full essential image, including every higher simplex of every diagram.

source.place: Agent conclusion proving this specialization of Theorem 4.8.4.1 through the local adjoint criterion; componentwise equivalences yield coherent natural equivalences.

proof_origin.place: Agent proof of the essential-image specialization of Theorem 4.8.4.1, via Kerodon 6.2.6.1 (02FV) and 6.2.1.17 (02F1), existing mapping-composition, simplicial-homotopy-invariance and componentwise-equivalence DAG tools. Step 2 writes both inverse homotopies explicitly, avoiding the cyclic mapping-bifunctor dependency. The online sources are not archived in literature/.
